description: Memory pressure: available vs commit, paging and swap activity, kernel pool growth and cache composition. Low Available % plus rising page faults means the host is trimming working sets.

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Critical. Windows is trimming working sets and allocations will start failing. Free RAM or move workload.
panels.title: Available < 10%

panels.description: Warning band - act before it reaches 10%.
panels.title: Available < 15%

panels.description: Committed memory close to the commit limit. Grow the pagefile or add RAM to avoid allocation failures.
panels.title: Commit > 85%

panels.description: Worst host right now.
panels.title: Min Available %

panels.description: Typical host. A low median means the whole fleet is undersized.
panels.title: Median Available %

panels.description: Highest commit charge against the commit limit.
panels.title: Max Commit %

panels.description: High page-fault rate. Combined with swap traffic it means real paging to disk, not just soft faults.

panels.description: Total physical memory in the current selection.
panels.title: Fleet RAM

panels.description: Start here - these hosts are closest to memory exhaustion.

panels.description: Commit pressure is about the pagefile + RAM budget, not just free RAM.

panels.description: Cross-check with swap read/write below to tell soft faults from real paging.
panels.title: Highest Page Faults/s (topk 15)

panels.description: Sorted lowest-available first. Nonpaged pool that keeps growing is a driver leak; paged pool growth is usually a service leak.
panels.title: Memory Health by Host

panels.description: Add RAM, cap the biggest consumer (see Collector process), or move a workload off these hosts.
panels.title: Hotspots: Available < 15%

panels.description: Commit pressure without low Available % usually means the pagefile is too small - see Collector pagefile.
panels.title: Hotspots: Commit > 85%

panels.description: A steady downward slope is a leak; a sawtooth is normal cache behaviour. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Available % (bottomk 10)

panels.description: Commit charge relative to the commit limit over time.
panels.title: Commit % (topk 10)

panels.description: Mostly soft faults on a healthy host. Compare with swap traffic to spot real paging.
panels.title: Page Faults/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Non-zero swap reads are the definitive sign that the host is paging from disk.
panels.title: Swap Read / Write per second (topk 10)

panels.description: Monotonic growth over days = kernel/driver memory leak. Restart or patch the offending driver.
panels.title: Kernel Pool Bytes (topk 10)

panels.description: A large modified page list means dirty pages are waiting to be written - usually storage backpressure.
panels.title: Cache Composition (fleet totals)

panels.description: Exhausting PTEs causes hard allocation failures even with free RAM. Rare, but fatal when it happens.
panels.title: Free System Page Table Entries (bottomk 10)

panels.description: New page allocations. Spikes track process start-up and large buffer allocation.
panels.title: Demand Zero Faults/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Pages recovered from standby - cheap faults, they do not touch disk.
panels.title: Transition Faults/s (topk 10)

panels.description: File cache misses. High rates mean the working set does not fit in cache.
panels.title: Cache Faults/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Breakdown of where physical memory actually sits on each host.
panels.title: Memory Composition Detail

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Scrape Duration (topk 10)
